edit.find: In the vanilla layout it is the B button (remapB); in this build transforms.json rewrites the system_init defaults to remapA = $8080 and remapB = $4008, so the A button feeds it (together with the attack bit $0080).
edit.with: The button that feeds it follows the remap table ($0DA6-$0DB4): in the vanilla Type 1 map (the table after a new game or a slot load) physical A gives $8000 and physical B gives $4000; in the identity map (title screen, diary, Button Type 2) physical B gives $8000. edit.find: Not traced: whether GetPlayerFacingDirection runs while row 8 is active.
edit.with: With $0AC8 = 8 forced and playerFlags bit 15 set, the call reads that word ($0100), subtracts the table address and adds the player animation frame; the long-indexed load then crosses from bank $83 into bank $84 offset $0100 + frame, which is the low WRAM page ($7E:0100 + frame, the stack page), not ROM, so the result is whatever that byte holds. Not traced: whether GetPlayerFacingDirection runs while row 8 is active.

edit.find: whether a caller can reach that case is not traced.
edit.with: FacingDirectionLookup holds 4 at the player animation frames $4A-$4F and $54-$57, and the Will ability table holds 4 at frames $18-$1A; the tracker tests neither the carry nor the range. Whether a tracker call coincides with one of those frames is not traced (observed in the Lily scene while the player walked: 10 calls, A = 1 or 2, carry clear).
